info.title: AI4Call Client API

1.2.0: Added public assistant identifiers while retaining legacy assistant API key compatibility.
Added Bearer authentication support for Client API business operations.
Added plugin-configuration routes scoped by stable instanceId.
Clarified assistant deletion safety and webhook payload documentation.
1.1.0: Hardened secret-field documentation with write-only provider API keys.
Expanded success examples, standard 500 responses and application error-code documentation.
Improved assistant, provider-wallet, knowledge, analytics, plugin and RAG schema documentation.
Added canonical audio-to-audio routes and payload aliases while preserving voice-to-voice compatibility.
Added canonical tenant paths for knowledge, filler phrase lists and RAG while keeping legacy /catalog aliases deprecated.
Added stable plugin instance identifiers with POST/PATCH/DELETE resource routes, assistant deletion and RAG collection create/delete.
Added opt-in cursor pagination to the main list resources without changing legacy unpaginated responses.
Preserved existing v1.1 authentication mechanisms and compatibility aliases without breaking changes.

info.description:
Public OpenAPI contract for the AI4Call client-facing APIs.

The primary service at `https://client-api.ai4call.com` covers authenticated account
management, assistants and their runtime configuration, provider wallet, catalog resources,
knowledge, RAG document management, tools and account analytics.

Current Client API authentication flow:
1. `POST /api/v1/auth/portal/login` validates `email` and `portalApiKey`. It does not
   issue an access token or create a server-side session.
2. Business calls accept `Authorization: Bearer <portalApiKey>` or the legacy pair
   `x-client-email` and `x-portal-api-key`.
3. Operations on a single assistant use `assistantId`; legacy `assistantApiKey` path values
   remain accepted during the v1 compatibility period.

This document also contains operations hosted by dedicated services. Public RAG operations
use their own Bearer authentication and outbound-call operations use their own API-key header;
each such operation declares its dedicated server and security scheme.

patch.summary: Update the configuration of a plugin instance
patch.description:
Update the configuration of a plugin instance using only human-readable names.

How to recover data:
- use `GET /api/v1/account/plugins/instances` to get `pluginName` and `instanceName`
- use `GET /api/v1/account/plugins/configuration?pluginName=...&instanceName=...` to read configurable fields and current values

PATCH semantics:
- `configuration` and merge-based: you can send only the fields to be modified or the entire object
- if you send `configuration.users`, the Telegram user list is completely replaced
- if you send `configuration.channels`, the Teams channel list is completely replaced

Configurable parameters for plugins:
- Email: `smtp_host`, `smtp_port`, `smtp_user`, `smtp_pass`, `smtp_security`, `from_name`, `test_mode_enabled`, `test_attempts_remaining`
- WhatsApp: `access_token`, `phone_number_id`, `template_name`, `test_mode_enabled`, `test_attempts_remaining`
- Telegram: `bot_token`, `enabled`, `users`
  `users` items: `{ "chat_id": "...", "username": "...", "firstName": "...", "lastName": "..." }`
- Teams: `method`, `webhook_url`, `client_id`, `client_secret`, `tenant_id`, `channels`
  `channels` items: `{ "channel_name": "...", "channel_id": "...", "webhook_url": "...", "team_id": "..." }`
- Condomatica: `api_key`, `codice_amministratore`, `enabled`
- n8n: `url`, `auth_type`, `auth_value`, `enabled`
- Zapier: `url`, `enabled`
- Zammad: `url`, `apiKey`, `enabled`
- Calendly: `bearerToken`, `enabled`
- CalDAV Apple: `apple_id`, `app_password`, `enabled`
- CalDAV Zimbra: `url`, `email`, `password`, `enabled`
- Assieasy: `username`, `password`, `secret`, `smtpInstanceName`, `enabledTools`
  `smtpInstanceName` must match `instanceName` of an active instance of the Email plugin taken from `GET /api/v1/account/plugins/instances`
  `enabledTools` shape: `{ "search_by_phone": true, "get_documents": true, "send_document": false, "get_policies": true }`

post.summary: Save a new credential in the wallet
post.description:
Saves a provider credential. The value is encrypted at rest and never returned in clear text.

How to build the payload:
- read `GET /api/v1/account/provider-wallet/catalog`
- copy `serviceType`, `provider` and `engine` from the chosen entry
- fill `config` with the keys listed in that entry's `fields`

Operational rules:
- `config` accepts only the declared keys: any other key returns `400`
- every field marked `required` must be present and non-empty
- fields with `options` accept only the listed values
- `name` is free text, used to recognise the credential later

The `id` in the response is the value to use as `providerWalletId` on the assistant runtimes.

post.summary: Create a new pre-initialized assistant for the authenticated client
post.description:
Creates the assistant by replicating the same logic used by the AI4Call portal.

For a classic assistant only `name` and `description` are required.
For an audio-to-audio assistant send `mode: audio_to_audio` and, if you want
to override the defaults, the canonical `audioToAudio` block.
The legacy `voice_to_voice` mode and `voiceToVoice` field remain accepted for compatibility.

The backend automatically performs:
- `assistantApiKey` generation in `ai4call_sk_*` format
- progressive `jsonFilename` allocation in `FLLM*.json` format
- demo `virtualNumber` generation in `0000********` format
- runtime JSON initialization with portal defaults
- backend provisioning trigger
- best-effort attempt to register the assistant on the MCP tenant

Initial defaults applied:
- TTS `tts_live_azure_multi` with voice `it-IT-ElsaNeural`
- ASR `asr_azure_multi`
- LLM `openai` with model `gpt-4o`
- first message not configured (empty `firstMessage.text`)
- preconfigured initial prompt
- initial status `draft`

If `mode` is `audio_to_audio`, the backend initializes a
`configType: voice-llm` JSON with an audio-to-audio root compatible with the portal.

get.summary: Retrieve editable prompt and configuration of the assistant's first message
get.description:
Returns the prompt configuration of the assistant in the same conceptual model used by the portal.

### What comes back
- `prompt.text`: only the editable part of the prompt
- `firstMessage.text`: the first static message, if present
- `firstMessage.callerSpeaksFirst`: option that indicates whether the caller speaks first
- `firstMessage.uninterruptible`: option that indicates whether the first message cannot be interrupted

### Important note
Any automatic sections already present in the JSON, such as system blocks or knowledge, are not returned in `prompt.text`.
On `voice_to_voice` servers, `prompt.text` corresponds to the root field `prompt` of the JSON `voice-llm`; the first message is not used.

patch.summary: Update the hangup tool schema configuration
patch.description:
Update hangup schema configuration with `PATCH merge` semantics.

Editable parameters:
- `hangupUrl`
- `schema`
- `schema[].name`
- `schema[].type`
- `schema[].description`
- `schema[].required`
- `schema[].enumValues`
- `schema[].children`

How to recover current data:
- use `GET /api/v1/assistants/{assistantApiKey}/runtime/hangup/schema`

---

### Operational rules

- At least one between `hangupUrl` and `schema` must be present in the bodysuit
- Omitted fields retain the current value
- Sending `schema` **completely replaces** the current schema (it is not a merge)
- Sending `hangupUrl: null` removes the URL webhook, disables the hangup tool **and also automatically clears the schema**
- Sending `schema: []` clears the scheme keeping the current URL

---

- On assistants `voice_to_voice`, the backend updates `pbxTools.hangupEndpoint.endpoint` and `pbxTools.hangupEndpoint.input_schema`

### How to build the schema body

The `schema` is an array of **properties** that define the fields of the sent JSON body
to `hangupUrl` at the end of the call. Each property has the following structure:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | `string` | yes | Field name in JSON body |
| `type` | `string` | yes | Field Type: `string`, `number`, `boolean`, `enum`, `object` |
| `description` | `string` | no | Field Description (helps the LLM model understand what to enter) |
| `required` | `boolean` | no | If `true`, the field is required in the body hangup |
| `enumValues` | `string[]` | only for `enum` | List of allowed values ​​(only if `type: enum`) |
| `children` | `Property[]` | only for `object` | Nested fields (only if `type: object`) |

---

### Supported types and how to use them

**`string`** — free text field:
```json
{ "name": "motivo", "type": "string", "description": "Motivo del termine della chiamata", "required": true }
```

**`number`** — numeric field:
```json
{ "name": "durata_secondi", "type": "number", "description": "Durata della chiamata in secondi" }
```

**`boolean`** — boolean field:
```json
{ "name": "cliente_soddisfatto", "type": "boolean", "description": "Il cliente si è dichiarato soddisfatto" }
```

**`enum`** — multiple choice field, requires `enumValues`:
```json
{ "name": "esito", "type": "enum", "description": "Esito della chiamata", "required": true, "enumValues": ["positivo", "negativo", "richiamata"] }
```

**`object`** — nested field group, requires `children`:
```json
{
  "name": "dati_cliente",
  "type": "object",
  "description": "Dati raccolti durante la chiamata",
  "children": [
    { "name": "nome", "type": "string", "description": "Nome del cliente" },
    { "name": "email", "type": "string", "description": "Email del cliente" }
  ]
}
```

---

### Example of resulting JSON body

With the above scheme, the webhook will receive a body similar to:
```json
{
  "motivo": "Cliente ha chiesto informazioni sul prodotto X",
  "esito": "positivo",
  "cliente_soddisfatto": true,
  "durata_secondi": 182,
  "dati_cliente": {
    "nome": "Mario Rossi",
    "email": "mario@example.com"
  }
}
```

get.summary: Retrieve the calling number verification configuration
get.description:
Returns the current configuration of the webhook used to verify the number
caller before the call is connected to the assistant.

If no configuration has been created yet, `data.configuration` will be `null`.

### How number verification works

When a call arrives, the system makes an HTTP request to the configured webhook,
passing the calling number into the indicated field (`numberParamName`), in the position
indicated (`numberLocation`). The webhook should respond with:

```json
{ "enabled": true }
```

- If `enabled` is `true` (or absent): the call continues normally
- If `enabled` is `false`: the call is blocked

The webhook can also return an `callerInfo` object with additional data that
will be made available to the assistant during the call.

### Safety note

Sensitive fields (`authToken`, `authPassword`) are never returned in clear text.
In their place there are the flags `hasAuthToken` and `hasAuthPassword`.

patch.summary: Create or update the calling number verification configuration
patch.description:
Create the configuration if it does not exist, otherwise update the fields provided
with **PATCH merge** semantics (omitted fields retain the current value).

Editable parameters:
- `name`
- `method`
- `url`
- `numberLocation`
- `numberParamName`
- `headersJson`
- `authType`
- `authToken`
- `authUsername`
- `authPassword`
- `timeoutMs`
- `isActive`

How to recover current data:
- use `GET /api/v1/assistants/{assistantApiKey}/runtime/precall/number-validation`

---

### Operational rules

- At least one field must be present in the body
- Omitted fields retain the current value (or the default if it is the first creation)
- Send `isActive: false` **completely deletes** the configuration — `data.configuration` will be `null`
- The configuration is always active (`isActive: true`) when it is created or updated
- Sending `authToken: null` removes the configured token
- Sending `authPassword: null` removes the configured password
- Sending `headersJson: null` removes all custom headers
- **`authToken` and `authPassword` are never returned** — use `hasAuthToken`/`hasAuthPassword`

---

### How to configure `numberLocation`

| Value | Where the number is sent | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `query` | URL query string | `GET /validate?caller_id=0391234567` |
| `body` | Body JSON of the request | `POST /validate` with leotard `{ "caller_id": "0391234567" }` |
| `params` | URL segment | `GET /validate/0391234567` (the number replaces `:numberParamName` in the URL) |

---

### Authentication supported

| `authType` | Required fields | Header generated |
|---|---|---|
| `none` | — | none |
| `bearer` | `authToken` | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` |
| `api_key` | `authToken` | `X-Api-Key: <token>` |
| `basic` | `authUsername` + `authPassword` | `Authorization: Basic <base64>` |

---

### Expected response from webhook

The webhook must respond with HTTP 200 and a JSON body containing at least:
```json
{ "enabled": true }
```

May include additional data:
```json
{
  "enabled": true,
```

get.description:
Returns the current configuration of the pre-call phase:
general settings (`configuration`) and associated tools (`tools`).

### How the pre-call phase works

Before the call is connected to the assistant, the system performs sequentially
the configured tools (in the order defined by `order`). The tools can be:
- **custom tools** (defined in the server JSON, `subscriptionName: null`)
- **tool MCP plugin** or **custom MCP** (with `subscriptionName` enhanced)

The tools can retrieve caller information, perform validation or
enrich the context, and end the call early if
`earlyTerminationEnabled` is `true`.

If `waitingAudioText` is configured, it is played to the caller during execution.
`voiceConfig` controls the voice used to generate wait/terminate audio,
while `modelConfig` controls the model used to interpret the results of the tools.

The fields `toolName` and `subscriptionName` returned match the fields
`toolName` and `subscriptionName` to send in the PATCH.
The pre-call tools can only be chosen from those already associated with the assistant:
- `GET /api/v1/catalog/assistants/{assistantApiKey}/tools`

patch.description:
Update pre-call configuration with **PATCH merge** semantics.
At least one field must be present in the bodysuit.

Editable parameters:
- `tools`
- `tools[].toolName`
- `tools[].subscriptionName`
- `tools[].order`
- `globalPrompt`
- `waitingAudioText`
- `earlyTerminationEnabled`
- `terminationMessage`
- `waitingAudioNonInterruptible`
- `modelConfig`
- `voiceConfig`

How to retrieve the current configuration:
- `GET /api/v1/assistants/{assistantApiKey}/runtime/precall/mcp-config`

---

### Tool management

The `tools` field **completely replaces** the current pre-call tools:

| Body posted | Effect |
|---|---|
| `tools` omitted | keeps current tools unchanged |
| `tools: []` | removes all pre-call tools and resets all pre-call configuration |
| `tools: [{...}]` | replaces with the sent list |

For sorting:
- if each item includes `order`, `order` is used
- if `order` is omitted, array order is used

---

### How to build the `tools` list

Use the records of `GET /api/v1/catalog/assistants/{assistantApiKey}/tools` to get `toolName` and `instanceName`.
The pre-call only accepts tools already associated with the assistant:

| Tool type | `toolName` | `subscriptionName` |
|---|---|---|
| `custom_tool` (custom JSON tool) | `toolName` | `null` |
| `plugin_tool` (MCP plugin) | `toolName` | `instanceName` |
| `custom_mcp_tool` (MCP custom) | `toolName` | `instanceName` |

The custom tools (`subscriptionName: null`) are those defined in the assistant's JSON
and they do not require subscriptions.

---

### General configuration

| Field | Effect |
|---|---|
| `globalPrompt: null` | removes the global prompt |
| `waitingAudioText: null` | removes hold audio |
| `earlyTerminationEnabled: true` | enable early termination |
| `terminationMessage: null` | removes termination message |
| `waitingAudioNonInterruptible: false` | makes hold audio interruptible |
| `modelConfig` | set default/assistant/managed/custom for pre-call model |
| `voiceConfig` | set default/assistant/custom for pre-call TTS |
